The '''Vande Bharat''' trainset, formerly known as '''Train 18''', is an Indian [[electric multiple unit]] designed for [[Vande Bharat Express|Vande Bharat]] train services of the [[Indian Railways]]. It was designed and developed by the state-owned [[Integral Coach Factory]] in [[Chennai]].

The trainsets consist of eight, sixteen or twenty air-conditioned [[chair car]] coaches. Introduced in 2018, the trainsets achieved speeds of up to {{cvt|183|km/h}} during trial runs, and has a maximum operational speed of {{cvt|160|km/h}} in regular service.<ref>{{cite web |date=3 April 2023 |title=Bhopal Delhi Vande Bharat Express: Top speed of 160 kmph! Is food free in Delhi to Bhopal semi high-speed train? Know time, route, ticket price |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/business-economy/industry/bhopal-delhi-vande-bharat-express-top-speed-of-160-kmph-is-food-free-in-delhi-to-bhopal-semi-high-speed-train-know-time-route-ticket-price-article-99210203 |access-date=3 April 2023 |work=[[Times Now]]}}</ref>

==History==
=== Dawn of EMUs ===
{{See also|Multiple units of India}}

[[File:Inaugural train at Victoria Terminus, Bombay.jpg|thumb|left|Inaugural EMU train at Victoria Terminus, Bombay, on the erstwhile GIP, now [[Central Railway zone]]]]
<!--[[File:Eight Coach Electric Train approaching Kurla.jpg|thumb|Eight Coach EMU train approaching Kurla]]-->

The first [[electric multiple unit]] (EMU) technology in India was introduced in Mumbai as a [[Commuter rail|suburban railway]] service on 3 February 1925.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/mumbai/age-is-just-a-number-she-can-keep-mumbais-life-on-track-even-at-90/|title=Age is just a number, she can keep Mumbai's life on track even at 90|work=The Indian Express|date=9 February 2015}}</ref> With an increase in demand post-independence, India began to import EMUs from [[Europe]] and [[Japan]], before it could manufacture indigenously. In the 1960s, [[Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited|BHEL]], an Indian public sector giant started manufacturing electrical equipment for indigenous EMUs, which then started entering service in the same decade.<ref name="EMU_History">{{Cite web |date=15 October 1999 |title=Electrical Multiple Units |url=https://st2.indiarailinfo.com/kjfdsuiemjvcya1/0/8/0/2/4684802/1/multipleunits1091923.pdf |website=Indian Rail Info }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Historical Background of Railway Electrification |url=https://core.indianrailways.gov.in/view_section.jsp?lang=0&id=0,294,302,530#:~:text=The%20first%20electric%20train%20ran,electrified%20on%201500%20Volt%20DC. |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=core.indianrailways.gov.in}}</ref> During the same time, [[Integral Coach Factory]] of [[Chennai]], a government-owned manufacturer of rail coaches started developing EMUs indigenously. This is regarded as a major leap in the Indian railway industry as they became the earliest precursors to Vande Bharat technology.<ref name="EMU_History"/>

[[File:Adra asansol MEMU.JPG|thumb|left|[[Adra Junction railway station|Adra]] – [[Asansol]] MEMU, the first MEMU service in India which began operation in 1995]]
<!--[[File:Palakkad Erode MEMU.jpg|thumb|[[Palakkad]] – [[Erode]] MEMU]]-->

By the 1990s, [[Indian Railways]] had a large number of EMU trainsets within the cities of Chennai, Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai on their suburban railways. For regular long-distance travel, India continued relying on [[Locomotives of India|locomotives]]. The inefficiency of these locomotive-hauled trains was soon felt while the developed world already had well-built EMU [[High-speed rail|high-speed technology]] by the 1990s. EMUs for longer distances were conceived on the long-distance main lines, which led to the development of [[MEMU|mainline electric multiple units]] (MEMU). With the advantages of faster acceleration-deceleration, presence of driver cabins at both ends, being energy efficient with [[regenerative braking]], encouraged Indian Railways to develop MEMUs for distances beyond the suburban belt.<ref name="EMU_History"/> A decade later, India had several MEMUs operating across the country's electrified routes as a short-distance inter-city service. However, India still had to rely on locomotives for medium and long-distance travel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MEMU |url=https://www.irfca.org/gallery/Suburban/MEMU/ |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=irfca.org}}</ref>

=== Need for speed and comfort ===
For most of Indian Railways' history, speed and comfort were not of primary concern as safety was of utmost importance. While India saw 325 accidents in 2003–04, this number was down to 106 in 2015–16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=What Explains the High Number of Railway Accidents? |url=https://thewire.in/uncategorised/railway-safety-accident-derailment |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=The Wire}}</ref> The replacement of old [[ICF coach]]es by the modern and safer [[LHB coach]]es also helped the cause significantly.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 June 2014 |title=LHB coaches reduced number of casualties |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/415982/lhb-coaches-reduced-number-casualties.html |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref> During the same period, Indian Railways had introduced [[Gatimaan Express|Gatimaan]] and [[Tejas Express|Tejas]] services that enhanced comfort with their modern LHB coaches. As the next step, Indian Railways at [[Integral Coach Factory|ICF]] headed by general manager Sudhanshu Mani, started designing a new [[Electric multiple unit|EMU]] trainset that was set to be developed at half the imported cost.  Since these trains were planned to be ready by 2018, they were named 'Train-2018' and later 'Train 18'. They were designed to be fully air-conditioned and equipped with automatic doors, onboard Wi-Fi, and infotainment and many other modern facilities. It would mark the beginning of a new era in the Indian Railways where modern EMUs for long distances beyond suburban railways started plying.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 February 2017 |title=Indian Railways to roll out 'Make in India' 160 kmph self-propelled 'world-class' train sets at half the cost of import! |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/indian-railways-to-roll-out-make-in-india-160-kmph-self-propelled-world-class-train-sets-at-half-the-cost-of-imports/558791/ |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=The Financial Express |language=en}}</ref> Train 18 was designed with the [[LHB coach]] as a base. With sixteen chair cars and a 160 km/h speed, the technology was set to replace [[Shatabdi Express|Shatabdi]] services.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 March 2018 |title=Indian Railways enters new league! Swanky 160 kmph engine-less Make in India train is too good; 15 features |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/photos/business-gallery/1112743/train-18-indian-railways-self-propelled-160kmph-speed-features-images-make-in-india/ |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=The Financial Express |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Railways to Replace Shatabdi Express with 'Made in India' Semi-High Speed, Engine-Less Train 18 {{!}} India.com |url=https://www.india.com/news/india/indian-railways-to-replace-shatabdi-express-with-made-in-india-semi-high-speed-engine-less-train-18-2968511/ |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=www.india.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Prototype and related issues ===

[[File:Vande Bharat Express on Platform 16 in New Delhi 02.jpg|thumb|left|First generation Vande Bharat on platform 16 in New Delhi]]

The manufacturing of Train 18 was coincidentally completed 18 months after initiation. It was built at a cost of {{INRConvert|970|m|lk=r|year=2018}} and had 80% indigenous components.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 October 2018 |title=Train 18: Country's first engine-less train rolled out; Train 20 next |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/train-18-countrys-first-engine-less-train-rolled-out-train-20-next/articleshow/66419774.cms |access-date=20 May 2023 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> During its trial runs, Train 18 became the fastest EMU train in India after attaining a speed of 180 km/h, during its test run at the Kota-Sawai Madhopur section.<ref>{{cite news |title=Train 18 Crosses Speed Limit During Trial Run, Is Now India's Fastest |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/indias-first-engineless-train-sets-new-speed-record-1956786 |access-date=16 August 2024 |work=NDTV.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Train 18: Top features and facilities of the country's 'fastest train' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/train-18-top-features-and-facilities-of-the-countrys-fastest-train/article62020243.ece |access-date=16 August 2024 |work=[[The Hindu]] |date=3 December 2018 |language=en-IN}}</ref> This speed was 4 km/h shy of India's overall best record of 184 km/h achieved by a [[Indian locomotive class WAP-5|WAP-5 Class locomotive]] back in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |title=[IRFCA] Evolution of High-Speed Haulage on Indian Railways |url=https://www.irfca.org/docs/high-speed-evolution.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=irfca.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=26 December 2018 |title=Train 18 becomes India's fastest train |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/train-18-to-officially-become-the-fastest-train-in-india/articleshow/67257150.cms |access-date=20 May 2023 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> Train 18 was renamed as 'Vande Bharat Express' as an acknowledgement for the fact that it was completely built in India by Indian engineers.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 January 2019 |title=Train 18 named Vande Bharat Express: Piyush Goyal |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/train-18-named-vande-bharat-express-piyush-goyal/articleshow/67709409.cms |access-date=20 May 2023 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Subramanian |first1=Lakshmi |title=Meet the makers of the Vande Bharat Express trains |url=https://www.theweek.in/theweek/business/2023/12/23/inside-the-integral-coach-factory-in-chennai-where-vande-bharat-express-trains-are-manufactured.html |access-date=27 December 2023 |work=The Week |language=en |quote=The Vande Bharat trains are a cause of much enthusiasm among railway travellers in India. Introduced as Train 18 in 2018 and renamed Vande Bharat Express ahead of its first service the following February, they are the first semi-high speed trains in India.}}</ref>

On 15 February 2019, the first Vande Bharat Express between [[New Delhi]] and [[Varanasi]] was flagged off at the [[New Delhi railway station]] by Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 February 2019 |title=Vande Bharat Express flagged off: How to book, fares and more |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/vande-bharat-express-flagged-off-how-to-book-fares-and-more/story-WJIT6vuRhVGZwf1jwdtnKJ.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref><ref name="VBE Inaugration">{{cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/economy-politics/train-18-pm-modi-to-flag-off-vande-bharat-express-on-february-15-from-new-delhi/story/317978.html|title=Train 18: PM Modi to flag off Vande Bharat Express on February 15 from New Delhi|work=Business Today|date=7 February 2019|access-date=17 February 2019}}</ref> The train ran from [[New Delhi]] to [[Varanasi]] via [[Kanpur]] and [[Allahabad|Prayagraj]], connecting Uttar Pradesh's [[Varanasi]] to the capital city and reduced the existing travel time along the route by 15%.<ref name="express24">{{citation |title=Train 18, India's first engine-less train, set to hit tracks on October 29 |date=24 October 2018 |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/train-18-indias-first-engine-less-train-set-to-hit-tracks-on-october-29-5415892/ |work=[[The Indian Express]]}}</ref> The 8-hour journey from New Delhi to Varanasi station covered a total distance of {{Cvt|762|km}} between the two cities. However, while returning from [[Varanasi]], the train broke down due to a cattle runover. According to reports, four cars of the train experienced an electrical outage and brakes were reported to be jammed as the train was halted for over an hour at [[Tundla Junction railway station]] before resumption.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vande Bharat Express hits a cow and breaks down on Day 1 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/a-day-after-launch-vande-bharat-express-breaks-down-while-returning-from-varanasi-1457476-2019-02-16 |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

The fleet of Vande Bharat trainsets was set to expand in numbers but Indian Railways had stopped the production of new sets owing to internal issues.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fresh Tender System For Vande Bharat Express After 'Favouritism Charges' |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/railways-introduces-fresh-tender-system-for-vande-bharat-express-after-favouritism-charges-2070639 |access-date=21 May 2023 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref> After the intervention of the Railway Minister, Railways decided to resume tenders for the production of new sets. However, they wished to provide more time so that the manufacturers could come up with the cheapest bid and because the train would require a major upgrade from scratch, as per one railway official.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 September 2019 |title=40 new Vande Bharat Express trains by 2022 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/40-new-vande-bharat-express-trains-by-2022/story-jOMnZOLenfRUpZeajC3D7O.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

The seven companies were Medha Servo Drives, [[Alstom]], [[Siemens]], [[Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited]] (BHEL), [[Titagarh Wagons]], Saini Electricals and CGL.<ref name="IRJ1">{{cite web |last1=Jha |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/infrastructure/sail-rinl-to-make-wheels-for-vande-bharat-express-trains-more-to-come-from-malaysia-us-china-13518432.htm |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 September 2022 |title=In a first, railways floats tender for a new plant to make 80,000 train wheels |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/in-a-first-railways-floats-tender-for-new-plant-to-make-80-000-train-wheels-101662740224242.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> On 9 September 2022, trial runs for the second version of Vande Bharat Express were completed,<ref name=":5" /> during which it broke the acceleration record as it accelerated from {{Cvt|0–100|km/h}} in just 52 seconds, making it two seconds faster than [[Shinkansen|Japanese bullet trains]] in acceleration.<ref name=":14">{{Cite news |title=With 100 KMPH Speed In 52 Seconds, Vande Bharat Express Beats Japanese Bullet Train |work=news18 |url=https://www.news18.com/news/auto/with-100-kmph-speed-in-52-seconds-vande-bharat-express-beats-japanese-bullet-train-6026509.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=15 September 2022 |title=Vande Bharat takes around 5 hours in Ahmedabad–Mumbai trial run, breaks bullet train record |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/mumbai-news/vande-bharat-takes-around-5-hours-in-ahmedabad-mumbai-trial-run-breaks-bullet-train-record/articleshow/94127912.cms |access-date=21 May 2023 |issn=0013-0389}}</ref> It entered service on 30 September 2022.<ref name=":9">{{cite web |date=30 September 2022 |title=Vande Bharat Express 2.0: PM flags off a new train between Gandhinagar and Mumbai, here's all to know |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/vande-bharat-express-20-pm-modi-flags-off-new-train-between-gandhinagar-and-mumbai-348690-2022-09-30 |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Business Today |language=en}}</ref>

In early 2023, an allocation was made for Vande Bharat services with a reduced car configuration, for lower demand, known as Mini Vande Bharat Express. It was projected to cost about {{INRConvert|650|m}} per rake for an 8-car configuration, at a cost of {{INRConvert|81.25|m}} per car. Indian Railways was targeting for manufacturing 1,000 Mini Vande Bharat rakes of 8-car configuration. During the financial year of 2023–24, an allocation of {{INRConvert|1|m}} had been made for designing the concept and preliminary research.<ref>{{cite news |date=6 February 2023 |title=8-car mini Vande Bharat trains get funds from budget; to run intercity |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/mumbai-news/8car-mini-vande-bharat-trains-get-funds-from-budget-to-run-intercity-101675623899853.html |access-date=8 April 2023 |work=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2023, Indian Railways announced a new saffron and grey livery for Vande Bharat trains inspired by the Indian tricolour.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/vande-bharats-new-look-inspired-by-tricolour-know-all-about-upgrades-made-in-train-2403973-2023-07-09 |title=Vande Bharat's new look inspired by Tricolour. Know all about upgrades made in train |date=9 July 2023 |access-date=14 July 2023 |work=India Today}}</ref> The Union Minister of Railways, Ashwini Vaishnaw, said that 25 improvements have been incorporated into the trains, including anti-climbing devices. These anti-climbing devices will also be added to trains other than Vande Bharat.

In August 2024, trial runs of 20-car Vande Bharat were conducted on the Mumbai–Ahmedabad route.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/watch-new-20-coach-vande-bharat-train-trial-run-conducted-on-mumbai-ahmedabad-route-faster-service-to-start-soon/articleshow/112422235.cms |title=Watch: New 20-coach Vande Bharat train trial run conducted on Mumbai–Ahmedabad route; Faster service to start soon |date=10 August 2024 |access-date=24 August 2024 |work=The Economic Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Engineering ==
[[File:Cabin of Vande Bharat Express.jpg|thumb|Cabin View of Vande Bharat Express trains]]
As part of the "[[Make in India]]" initiative, the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) created and produced the Vande Bharat Express.<ref>{{cite news |title=Seven companies bags order for 58 Vande Bharat trains |url=https://www.constructionworld.in/transport-infrastructure/metro-rail-and-railways-infrastructure/seven-companies-bags-order-for-58-vande-bharat-trains/33103 |work=Construction World |quote=Currently, two Vande Bharat Express trains are operational, and 44 are being manufactured at Integral Coach Factory (ICF), Chennai. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that 400 new semi-high-speed Vande Bharat trains would be rolled out in the next three years}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Porecha |first1=Maitri |title=Railways cancels ₹30,000 crore Vande Bharat tender as negotiations fail |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/railways-cancels-30000-crore-vande-bharat-tender-as-negotiations-fail/article68520987.ece |access-date=11 December 2024 |work=[[The Hindu]] |date=13 August 2024 |language=en-IN |quote=Integral Coach Factory and creator of the Vande Bharat train}}</ref> There are two generations of the train with design upgrades and addition of new features with subsequent generations.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Sanyal |first=Debarghya |date=1 December 2022 |title=Who's the brain behind Vande Bharat? |url=https://www.business-standard.com/podcast/current-affairs/who-s-the-brain-behind-vande-bharat-122120100513_1.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Business Standard |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |date=1 December 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Db6wS_ox1E |title=Who's the brain behind Vande Bharat? |work=[[Business Standard]] |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=15 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221202055717/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0Db6wS_ox1E |archive-date=2 December 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== First generation ===

[[File:Vande Bharat Express Economy Chair Car (interior).jpg|thumb|First generation Vande Bharat Chair Car (CC) seating]]

[[File:Vande Bharat Express Executive Chair Car (interior).jpg|thumb|First generation Vande Bharat Executive Chair Car (EC) seating]]

The exterior of the first version of Vande Bharat Express had an aerodynamic design that helped to reduce air resistance at high speeds.<ref name="ectimespti">{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/train-18-countrys-first-engine-less-train-rolled-out-train-20-next/articleshow/66419774.cms|title=Train 18: Country's first engine-less train rolled out; Train 20 next|date=29 October 2018|work=[[The Economic Times]]|access-date=5 November 2018}}</ref> It had a driver's cabin at each end, that enables immediate switch in train's direction, unlike a locomotive-hauled train.<ref name="unitedtrial">{{cite news|url=http://www.uniindia.com/news/india/self-propelled-train-18-debuts-for-trial-run/1391824.html|title=Self-propelled Train 18 debuts for trial run|date=29 October 2018|work=[[United News of India]]|access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref> The 16-car trainset weighs {{convert|430|t}} and has a seating capacity of 1,128 passengers.<ref name="shine">{{cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/indian-railways/the-crown-jewel-of-indian-railways-is-a-billion-rupee-made-in-india-train-118102900370_1.html|title=Train 18, India's first engine-less train, is also the country's fastest|last1=Shine|first1=Jacob|date=29 October 2018|work=[[Business Standard]]|access-date=4 November 2018|location=New Delhi, India}}</ref> Two of the centre compartments are first-class compartments that seat 52 each, with the rest being [[coach class|chair car]] compartments seating 78 each.<ref name="ndtv">{{cite news |date=29 October 2018 |title=Pics: Train 18 To Begin Trial Run Today. Here Are 10 Things To Know |work=[[NDTV Profit]] |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/train-18-indias-fastest-train-route-launch-date-today-features-engineless-rotating-seats-in-pictures-1939151 |access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref> The chassis of a coach is {{convert|23|m}} long, and the frame of the train is made entirely of stainless steel.<ref name=":4" /> Alternate coaches are motorised to ensure an even distribution of power and quicker acceleration and deceleration. The cars are interconnected and fully sealed to allow better mobility between coaches and reduce noise. The train features a GPS-based passenger information system, bio-vacuum toilets, and rotational seats that can be aligned in the direction of travel in the executive class,<ref>{{cite web |date=3 December 2018 |title=Train 18: Top features and facilities of the country's 'fastest train' |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/train-18-top-features-and-facilities-of-the-countrys-fastest-train/article25652410.ece |work=The Hindu}}</ref> and employs a [[regenerative braking]] system.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Prabhakar |first=Siddarth |date=9 December 2018 |title=ICF asked to make two more Train-18 rakes before Lok Sabha polls |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/icf-asked-to-make-two-more-train-18-rakes-before-ls-polls/articleshow/67006773.cms}}</ref>

This version reached a maximum speed of {{Cvt|180|km/h}}. It could accelerate to a speed of {{Cvt|100|km/h}} in 54.6 seconds and reach its maximum speed in 145 seconds. Trains were equipped with {{convert|24|in|cm|adj=on}} television screens that serve as the passenger information and entertainment system. The train's underframe electrical equipment can withstand floods up to {{Cvt|400|mm}}.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":10" /> Among the imported components were the wheels, seats, doors, braking system, transformers, and electronic parts such as processing chips.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Gupta |first=Moushumi Das |date=23 October 2022 |title=Hi-tech machines, 9,000+ workforce — inside Integral Coach Factory making Vande Bharat trains |url=https://theprint.in/india/hi-tech-machines-9000-workforce-inside-integral-coach-factory-making-vande-bharat-trains/1175653/ |access-date=24 October 2022 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="prabhakar">{{cite news |last1=Prabhakar |first1=Siddarth |date=23 October 2018 |title=First Made-in-India engineless train gets on track for trial run |work=[[The Times of India]] |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/first-made-in-india-train-set-ready-for-trial-run/articleshow/66324376.cms}}</ref>

=== Second generation ===
[[File:Vande Bharat Chair Car interior layout.jpg|thumb|Second generation Vande Bharat's Chair Car (CC) seating]]
[[File:Vande Bharat Executive Chair Car interior layout.jpg|thumb|Second generation Vande Bharat's Executive Chair Car (EC) seating]]
The second generation trains were built in 2022 and they could accelerate to a speed of {{Cvt|100|km/h}}<ref name=":131">{{Cite web |date=24 January 2023 |title=Vande Bharat Express Engine Type Power 0 to 100Km/h |url=https://vandebharat.com/article/vande-bharat-express-engine/ |access-date=24 January 2023 |website=Vande Bharat |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> in a record time of 52 seconds, compared to the 54 seconds taken by the older version. The train could reach a speed of {{Cvt|160|km/h}} in 140 seconds, 5 seconds faster than the first generation of the train. It is lighter, weighing {{convert|392|t}} compared to {{convert|430|t}} of the previous version, and is equipped with larger {{convert|32|in|cm|adj=on}} television screens and [[Wi-Fi]] on board. The air conditioning system on the VB2 utilises 15% less energy than the system on the first Vande Bharat trainset. VB2 also has automatic plug doors, sliding doors that don't need to be touched, emergency communication units, accessible toilets, a bigger driver's cabin, and seats in all coaches that can be leaned back.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=10 September 2022 |title=Vande Bharat train gets safety nod, likely to be flagged off on September 30 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/vande-bharat-train-gets-safety-nod-likely-to-be-flagged-off-on-september-30-101662834491749.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite web |date=29 November 2022 |title=Vande Bharat Express: Everything you need to know about the semi-high-speed train |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/travel/vande-bharat-express-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-semi-high-speed-train-15092861.htm |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=cnbctv18.com |language=en}}</ref> To address the seat reclining issues of the previous version, the new chairs were equipped with a push-back arrangement for smooth reclining.<ref name="Upgraded VBE" /><ref name="Upgraded VBE2" />

This version is additionally equipped for safety and protection with [[Kavach (train protection system)|Kavach]] signalling technology.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jha |first=Srinand |date=7 October 2022 |title=Indian Railways launches upgraded Vande Bharat EMU |url=https://www.railjournal.com/fleet/indian-railways-launches-upgraded-vande-bharat-emu/ |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=International Railway Journal |language=en-GB}}</ref> The train offers enhanced amenities, security, and surveillance systems, as well as features suited for emergencies. The seats are made up of fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) and were made by Tata Steel's Composites division.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.zeebiz.com/indian-railways/news-vande-bharat-express-features-route-speed-latest-news-update-details-features-tata-group-192097 | title=Vande Bharat Express to get aircraft-style passenger amenities – All details | date=August 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.lokmattimes.com/photos/national/indian-railways-vande-bharat-trains-to-getfirst-in-india-tata-steel-made-180-degrees-rotating-seats/ |title=Indian Railways: Vande Bharat trains to get 'First-in-India': Tata Steel-made 180 degrees rotating seats |date=1 August 2022 |access-date=18 April 2023 |work=[[Lokmat Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://currentaffairs.adda247.com/tata-steel-to-spend-3000-cr-on-seating-for-new-vande-bharat-trains/|title=TATA Steel to spend 3000 cr on seating for new Vande Bharat trains|first=Madhavi|last=Gaur|date=9 August 2022}}</ref> The new rolling stock features four emergency windows, disaster lights in all coaches in the event of lighting system failure, fire survival cables within door circuits, ventilation for three hours in the event that the air conditioner loses power, and four additional emergency push buttons per coach.<ref name="Upgraded VBE">{{cite web |date=20 August 2021 |title=Upgraded Vande Bharat trains with new features to be ready by 2022 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/upgraded-vande-bharat-trains-with-new-features-to-be-ready-by-2022-101629472505038.html |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref><ref name="Upgraded VBE2">{{cite web |date=20 August 2021 |title=New Vande Bharat Train Sets To Be Equipped For Emergency Evacuation |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/vande-bharat-express-new-vande-bharat-train-sets-to-be-equipped-with-features-to-aid-emergency-evacuation-2515206 |publisher=NDTV}}</ref> The new coaches are also equipped with a centralised coach-monitoring system for all types of electricity and climate control, among other new additions. An official added that the new coaches would be provided with a bacteria-free air conditioning system and higher flood protection for electrical equipment to ensure reliability during [[monsoon]]s up to {{cvt|650|mm}}.<ref name="Upgraded VBE" /><ref name="Upgraded VBE2" />

On 24 September 2023, 9 new Vande Bharat Express trains were flagged off which include upgraded features for passenger comfort after feedback.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/9-vande-bharat-trains-roll-out-with-new-feature-after-passenger-feedback/articleshow/103905681.cms |title=Nine Vande Bharat trains unveiled: What are the new upgraded features |date=24 September 2023 |work=The Times of India}}</ref> These include improvements to seats, improvements to toilets and an improved aerosol-based fire detection and suppression system.

==== Modified rakes ====
Several rakes have been modified to accommodate specific routes. The [[Mumbai CSMT–Sainagar Shirdi Vande Bharat Express]] and [[Mumbai CSMT–Solapur Vande Bharat Express]] are modified Vande Bharat trains that have additional parking brakes for stopping the train on a slope because they traverse sections of mountain passes. This feature is not available in other Vande Bharat trains.

The [[Ajmer–Delhi Cantonment Vande Bharat Express|Ajmer–Delhi Cantt. Vande Bharat express]] is a modified Vande Bharat train that has high-rise pantographs as the New Delhi–Jaipur route has a higher catenary for accommodating double-stacked containers and [[Double Decker Express]] trains.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/why-vande-bharat-express-train-is-being-modified-for-delhi-jaipur-route/articleshow/98860108.cms |title=Why Vande Bharat Express train is being modified for Delhi-Jaipur route |last=Jain |first=Smriti |date=1 March 2023 |access-date=16 April 2023 |work=[[The Times of India]]}}</ref> It is the world's first semi-high-speed passenger train with high-rise pantographs.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/jaipur/pm-narendra-modi-flags-off-rajasthans-first-vande-bharat-express-train-delhi-ajmer-jaipur-gurgaon/articleshow/99426168.cms |title=PM Narendra Modi flags off Delhi-Ajmer Vande Bharat Express |date=12 April 2023 |access-date=16 April 2023 |work=[[The Times of India]] |location=New Delhi}}</ref>

[[Srinagar–SMVD Katra Vande Bharat Express|Srinagar–Katra Vande Bharat Express]] has specially designed heated coaches tailored specifically for sub-zero weather environments. It's also equipped with defrosting heaters embedded in the driver’s windshield, the train ensures unobstructed sight-lines even in the harshest winter conditions.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2025-01-08 |title=Railways unveils Vande Bharat, specially designed for winters in J&K, for Katra–Srinagar route |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jammu-and-kashmir/railways-unveils-vande-bharat-specially-designed-for-winters-in-jk-for-katra-srinagar-route/article69075026.ece}}</ref>

== Future ==
The following [[Electric multiple unit|EMU]] trainsets which are influenced by the Vande Bharat are currently in the preliminary stages of design and will be introduced in the near future.

=== Sleeper trainsets ===
{{Main|Vande Bharat Sleeper Express}}
[[File:Vande_Bharat_sleeper_trainset_prototype_at_BEML.jpeg|thumb|[[Vande Bharat Sleeper Express|Vande Bharat Sleeper]] prototype by [[BEML]]]]
The sleeper EMU trainsets are being built with [[Sleeping car|sleeper coaches]] for long-distance travel. They will have three classes: 1A, 2A and 3A. The train is expected to have a maximum speed of {{Cvt|220|km/h}} and a design life of 35 years.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://zeenews.india.com/railways/vande-bharat-express-to-soon-get-220-kmph-top-speed-indian-railways-working-on-new-trains-2615998.html | title=Upcoming Vande Bharat Sleeper to Get 220 KMPH Top Speed, Indian Railways Working on New Trains }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/railways/sleeper-version-of-vande-bharat-train-will-be-designed-to-travel-at-220-km-per-hour-officials/97172720 | title=Sleeper version of Vande Bharat train will be designed to travel at 220 km per hour: Officials - ET Infra }}</ref><ref name="Apr 27">{{Cite web |author=Dipak K. Dash|date=27 April 2022 |title=Railways invites bids for 200 Vande Bharat trains with sleeper coaches for long-distance travel |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/railways-invites-bids-for-200-vande-bharat-trains-with-sleeper-coaches-for-long-distance-travel/articleshow/91133641.cms |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> It is expected to be lighter, energy efficient as well as have better passenger amenities than the Vande Bharat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Railways plans speedy roll-out of improved Vande Bharat fleet |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/india/railways-plans-speedy-roll-out-of-improved-vande-bharat-fleet |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}}</ref> Half of the trainsets will have coaches made of steel, while the other half will have coaches made of aluminium with [[Bogie#Articulated bogie|articulated bogies]].<ref>{{Cite web |author=Dipak K. Dash|date=21 July 2022 |title=Railways floats tender to procure 100 Vande Bharat trains with a maximum design speed of 200 km/h |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/railways-floats-tender-to-procure-100-vande-bharat-trains-with-maximum-design-speed-of-200-kmph/articleshow/93013529.cms |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref>

Indian Railways invited bids to design and manufacture 200 trainsets in April 2022. The agency estimated that it would cost {{INRConvert|260|b|year=2022}}.<ref name="Apr 27"/> The estimate includes the cost of upgrading infrastructure at either the Marathwada Rail Coach Factory in [[Latur]] or ICF where the train is planned to be manufactured.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Railways extends deadline for bids for 200 third-generation Vande Bharat train sets to October |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/indian-railways-extends-deadline-for-bids-for-200-third-generation-vande-bharat-train-sets-to-october-8792981.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Moneycontrol |date=7 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref> A further {{INRConvert|320|b|year=2022}} will be paid to the winning bidders over a 35-year period for maintenance. The bidders would be required to build the first prototype of this trainset within 24 months of being awarded the contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Livemint |date=1 December 2022 |title=BHEL bids for ₹58,000 cr deal to manufacture, maintain 200 Vande Bharat trains |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/bhel-bids-for-rs-58-000-crore-deal-to-maintain-200-vande-bharat-trains-11669900197456.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

=== Gati Shakti Train (Cargo Variant) ===

It is also known as '''Freight EMU''', supposedly to be used mainly to carry parcels of e-commerce companies, which is presently done via roadways. Indian Railways is planning to build 25 such trainsets to augment its freight market share in freight logistics from 28% to 40% by 2030 as a part of the government's "PM Gati Shakti" initiative.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sharma |first=Shantanu Nandan |title=Railways eyeing lucrative ecommerce space, making Vande Bharat-like freight trains that can run at 160 kmph |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/railways-eyeing-lucrative-ecommerce-space-making-vande-bharat-like-freight-trains-that-can-run-at-160-kmph/articleshow/91224847.cms |access-date=2022-08-22}}</ref> In October 2022, Indian Railway announced that [[Integral Coach Factory|ICF]] is designing the cargo version of Vande Bharat which will be tested by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) before final commissioning. The freight EMU rakes could reach an operational speed of 160 kmph and the rakes are being designed for palletized container transportation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nandi |first=Tamal |date=12 October 2022 |title=Now, Railways to introduce Vande Bharat' type freight trains. Check details |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/indian-railways-to-introduce-vande-bharat-freight-trains-on-delhi-mumbai-routes-11665547275905.html |access-date=31 March 2026 |website=livemint.com}}</ref> In March 2026, Indian Railway said that they are testing the first prototype where they will test multiple checks, including oscillation testing, emergency braking distance (EBD) evaluation and full-load performance assessments. The first prototype of 16-car EMU rake is designed to carry weight up to 264 tonnes at a maximum speed of 160 km/h.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mangla |first=Khushi |date=30 March 2026 |title=India's freight transport set for major upgrade: First Vande Bharat Cargo train to undergo trials this week |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/railways/indias-freight-transport-set-for-major-upgrade-first-vande-bharat-cargo-train-to-undergo-trials-this-weeknbsp/4189093/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |website=financialexpress.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Banarjee |first=Bikram |date=30 March 2026 |title=নতুন মাইলফলক ভারতীয় রেলের, চালু হচ্ছে দেশের প্রথম বন্দে ভারত মালগাড়ি |trans-title=New milestone for Indian Railways, country's first Vande Bharat freight train is being launched |url=https://indiahood.in/news/india/vande-bharat-cargo-memu-to-launch-bkm-30-03/366821/ |website=indiahood.in |access-date=1 April 2026 |language=bn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Saini |first=Kapil |date=30 March 2026 |title=Milestone for Railways: ICF to roll out India's first Vande Bharat Freight train for RDSO trials |url=https://metrorailnews.in/railways-to-launch-vande-bharat-freight-train/ |access-date=31 March 2026 |website=metrorailnews.in}}</ref>

=== Tilting technology ===
The [[Tilting train|tilting technology]] which aids the train in maintaining its speed on the curved sections is likely to be implemented in the future EMU trainsets which are planned to have a maximum speed of more than {{Cvt|200|km/h}}.<ref name="Surabhi">{{Cite web |last=Surabhi |date=17 July 2022 |title=Railways floats fresh tender for 200 next generation Vande Bharat trains |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/logistics/railways-to-ramp-up-production-of-vande-bharat-trains/article65650715.ece |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=Business Line |language=en}}</ref> This will mark the first commercial deployment of such technology in India.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 November 2022 |title=India to get 100 Vande Bharat trains with technology to tilt on turns by 2025 |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/india/india-to-get-100-vande-bharat-trains-with-technology-to-tilt-on-turns-by-2025-11669381957660.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=India to soon get tilting trains! |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/travel//india-to-soon-get-tilting-trains/articleshow/95849369.cms |access-date=5 December 2022 |newspaper=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> The coaches are proposed to be made of a lightweight aluminium alloy and are expected to feature improved passenger amenities such as a 3-pin socket and USB power socket for every passenger, zero discharge toilet systems, and facilities to accommodate passengers travelling in wheelchairs. The trains will also have a cattle guard that can absorb collisions with animals up to {{Convert|600|kg|lb|abbr=off}} in weight and keep animals from being dragged under the train in the event of a collision.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |date=18 July 2022 |title=Aluminium-Bodied, Speed of 200 Km/Hour: Govt Invites Tenders for 4th-Gen 200 Vande Bharat Trains|url=https://www.news18.com/news/india/aluminium-bodied-speed-of-200-kmhour-govt-invites-tenders-for-4th-gen-200-vande-bharat-trains-5575543.html |access-date=5 December 2022 |website=News18 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Other variants ===
{{Further|Namo Bharat Rapid Rail}}
The ICF is developing variants for suburban and short-distance services. The suburban variant is a 15-coach train with a carrying capacity of 6,000 people. The short distance variant that will replace existing [[MEMU]] services, will have eight coaches with a carrying capacity of 2,400 people.<ref name="nsection">{{cite news |title=ICF Chennai to manufacture prototype of Vande Bharat sleeper coach by end of this financial year |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/chennai/integral-coach-factory-chennai-to-manufacture-prototype-of-vande-bharat-sleeper-coach-train-to-be-ready-by-end-of-this-financial-year/article66896419.ece |access-date=27 December 2023 |work=The Hindu |date=26 May 2023 |language=en-IN |quote=The ICF is also designing a 15-coach Vande Bharat suburban train. The ICF is designing a prototype for the Vande Bharat Metro.}}</ref> As directed by the Indian Railway Board, the ICF will launch a model for Jammu and Kashmir in 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sivapriyan |first1=E |title=Integral Coach Factory to turn new Vande Bharat variants this fiscal |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/integral-coach-factory-to-turn-new-vande-bharat-variants-this-fiscal-2648770 |work=Deccan Herald |language=en |quote=To ensure that the Vande Bharat series is accessible and affordable to every section of the society, the ICF, as per directions from the Railway Board, will launch four new versions by next year, including an exclusive model for Jammu and Kashmir.}}</ref>

== Export ==
After the train's inauguration, Indian Railways reportedly received queries of interest from some countries in Southeast Asia and South America.<ref>{{cite news |date=21 May 2019 |title=Train 18 for exports after domestic demand is met: Railway official |language=en |work=Mint |url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/infrastructure/train-18-for-exports-after-domestic-demand-is-met-railway-official-1558452102971.html |access-date=17 April 2022}}</ref> A board member of the Indian Railways stated that the train could be modified according to customer needs.<ref>{{cite news |last=Jain |first=Smriti |date=18 January 2019 |title=Train 18 sets to be exported! Indian Railways looks to enter $200 billion world market for trains |work=The Financial Express |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/infrastructure/railways/train-18-sets-to-be-exported-indian-railways-looks-to-enter-200-billion-world-market-for-trains/1448035/ |access-date=18 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=PTI |date=18 January 2019 |title=Many Countries Interested in Importing India's Train 18 Set: Railway Officials |publisher=NDTV |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/many-countries-interested-in-importing-indias-train-18-set-railway-officials-1979857 |access-date=18 January 2019}}</ref> A railways official stated in November 2022 that the Ministry of Railways were preparing a roadmap to begin exports of Vande Bharat trainsets by 2026. Exports would only begin after 475 trainsets are built for domestic use.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news |last=Bhargava |first=Yuthika |date=26 November 2022 |title=Railways plans to export Vande Bharat trains by 2025–26 |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/railways-plans-to-export-vande-bharat-trains-by-2025-26/article66183627.ece |access-date=5 December 2022 |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

=== Test track ===
{{See also|List of railway test tracks}}
Indian Railways is constructing a {{Cvt|59|km}} long dedicated standard gauge track between Gudha and Thathana Mithri in the [[Jodhpur railway division|Jodhpur Division]] to conduct trial runs at speeds of up to {{Cvt|220|km/h}}. The track is expected to be completed by December 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-05-04 |title=India’s first high-speed rly test track in Raj to be ready by 2025 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/jaipur/indias-first-high-speed-railway-testing-track-in-rajasthan-to-be-ready-by-2025/articleshow/109828589.cms |access-date=2024-05-04 |work=Times of India}}</ref>

extract:
The Vande Bharat trainset, formerly known as Train 18, is an Indian electric multiple unit designed for Vande Bharat train services of the Indian Railways. It was designed and developed by the state-owned Integral Coach Factory in Chennai.
The trainsets consist of eight, sixteen or twenty air-conditioned chair car coaches. Introduced in 2018, the trainsets achieved speeds of up to 183 km/h (114 mph) during trial runs, and has a maximum operational speed of 160 km/h (99 mph) in regular service.
